claims.text: ``members`` are the nominal names an edge may point at, in SOURCE ORDER, deduplicated on first occurrence.
claims.why: The claim describes behaviour of members field; no code in this chunk implements deduplication or ordering logic.

claims.text: Union members and container elements both land here, because in both cases the answer to "what type does this position mention" is the same list; ``union`` says whether they are alternatives (and therefore need a shared ``union_id``) and ``containers`` says what shell they were wrapped in.
claims.why: No implementation of union/container logic in this chunk.

claims.text: ``None`` never becomes a member -- ``X | None`` is "optional X", not a union with a type called None -- and a bare ``Any`` never becomes a member either (see ``ANY_SENTINEL``).
claims.why: No logic for excluding None or Any from members in this chunk.

claims.text: A generic produces NO member per instantiation: ``list[User]`` is one edge to ``User`` with ``container == "list"``, so the type vocabulary stays bounded by the number of declarations instead of the number of call sites.
claims.why: No implementation of generic handling in this chunk.

claims.text: ``dropped`` holds nominal names the element rule deliberately discards -- mapping KEY types (``dict[str, User]`` -> ``User``, key dropped) and ``Callable`` parameter types. They are published so coverage can be honest about them; they are never edge targets.
claims.why: No implementation of dropped names logic in this chunk.

claims.text: A dotted name is kept VERBATIM (``ast.AST`` stays ``ast.AST``). Resolving it by its last segment would ask for a name called ``AST``, which nothing in such a file binds -- the module ``ast`` is what is bound.
claims.why: No implementation of dotted name handling in this chunk.

claims.text: These depth guards bound a malformed or adversarial input, they are not an expected limit (same posture as ``_declarator_name``'s ``range(16)``).
claims.why: The constants _ANN_DEPTH=16 and _STMT_DEPTH=64 are defined as depth guards.

claims.text: Parse ONE expression, or None. Never raises, never imports anything.
claims.why: The function uses try/except to catch SyntaxError, ValueError, RecursionError, MemoryError and returns None; no imports are done inside the function.

claims.text: The name an edge would point at, kept exactly as written.
claims.why: The function returns node.id for Name nodes, else ast.unparse(node) which preserves the written form.

observations.what: The comment mentions 'ANY_SENTINEL' but no such constant is defined in this chunk.

The _STRUCTURAL_NAMES set includes _UNION_NAMES, _TRANSPARENT, _SEQ_CONTAINERS, _MAP_CONTAINERS, _CALLABLE_NAMES but not _NONE_NAMES or _ANY_NAMES; this is consistent with the docstring that says structural names are syntactic only, while None/Any handling is a vocabulary judgement one layer up.
